title: Unzip an anti-static bag, take out an 18650 cell and stand it in a battery holder
instruction: With your left gripper, pull the bag's zipper slider all the way open. With your right gripper, take one yellow battery out of the bag and stand it, positive end up, in an empty cup of the battery holder, leaving the other battery in the bag. Then move both arms back to where they started.
context: Seating cells in holders is core work for electrical and electronic equipment assemblers and team assemblers on battery-pack lines: many times a shift they open the anti-static shielding bag the cells come in, take out one cell without disturbing the rest, and seat it in the pack's holder the right way up, since a reversed cell shorts the pack once it is welded.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Bag: a translucent grey metal-in static shielding stand-up pouch (100 mm wide, 99 mm tall, 34 mm gusset, printed ESD caution label) with a slider zipper along its top, zipped shut, its bottom glued to the table with its centre at (0.26, -0.02); its mouth runs along y, the slider at the right-hand end, pulled 77 mm toward the robot's left to open it. Inside stand two 18 x 65 mm 18650 lithium-ion cells (47 g, yellow wrap), positive ends up, 32 mm apart along the mouth. Holder: the black ABS bottom half of a 2x2 18650 holder (41.2 x 41.2 x 9.5 mm, 20 mm pitch, 0.3 mm radial clearance), empty, taped to the table with its centre at (0.30, -0.16), sides along x and y.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged from the video. (1) Bag unzipped: the slider pulled at least 90% of the way to its open end; counts once reached. (2) Battery taken out of the bag: a gripper holds a cell lifted clear of the bag (its lowest point at least 5 mm above the mouth); counts once reached. (3) Battery in the holder: with step 2 done, a cell stands in a cup of the holder within 3 mm of its seat, positive end up within 10 degrees, not held. (4) Other battery left in the bag: with step 2 done, a cell still stands in the bag (upright within 30 degrees), not held. Steps 3 and 4 are judged at the end. Full score 1.0, ending the run, only once all of these have held together without a break for 1 s: all four steps, both arms back where they started (within 3 cm) holding nothing, and the seated cell and the holder still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s). Any lapse, such as the cell moving faster, restarts that second; until the second is complete, all four steps score 0.8. 0 overall if at the end a cell or the holder has fallen off the table.
reset_notes: Stand the cell back in the bag at its mark, positive end up, and zip the bag shut (slider at its right-hand end).
fidelity: Articulated and rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The bag is one articulation glued down by its bottom: above it 8 film panels a side on sprung hinges (0.06 N m/rad), the slider a damped prismatic joint. The zipper's interlock is modelled by switching the panels' hinge targets from shut to open as the slider passes (a contact-only zipper was tried first). Film and slider collide as boxes and capsules, the holder as an SDF, each cell as a 30-sided prism.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms went to the bag early on and pressed at its top, then drew back near their bases, reaching toward it now and then; it never pulled the zipper open or took a cell out); demo: 1.0 (all four steps by step 601, success conditions from step 678, 1.0 at step 698)
